comments.body:
## `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` isolation is the EXPERIMENTAL CONTROL used to diagnose this. It is NOT the recommended fix. Do not read it as one.

Stating this at the top because the diagnosis and the remedy point in opposite directions, and
whoever picks this bug up will meet the diagnosis first.

**What the control proved.** Pointing `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` at a private directory and re-running
the eight affected modules gave 87 passed / 0 failed, against 29 failures on the shared one.
That cleanly separates "these tests contend with other processes' real gates" from "the code
under test is broken", and it settles attribution. That is all it was for.

**Why generalising it would be a serious regression.** The semaphore's entire purpose is to
bound TOTAL host gate concurrency (ADR 0112 decision 5) — `_slot_dir()` follows
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` precisely so one counter covers every process on the box. Per-session
isolation would give each session its own N slots. Six heavyweight rebar consumers were
observed on this machine on 2026-09-06; at the default cap that is up to **24 concurrent gates
on a 2-vCPU, 7813 MiB host**, against a measured ~714 MB peak per plan-review. The host has
room for two. That is the unbounded-composition defect epic `couped-subzero-wolf` exists to
fix, reintroduced one level down — and it would work by DELETING the bound while making the
symptom disappear, which is the worst combination available.

**The distinction the fix must preserve** — two different problems, two different answers:

| | should it consume a production gate slot? |
|---|---|
| a REAL gate run (`rebar review-plan`, a close gate), in any checkout | **YES** — one shared host-wide bound, exactly as today. Cross-checkout contention here is the feature. |
| a unit test exercising gate-adjacent code | **NO** — it is not real gate work, produces no verdict, spends none of the memory the bound exists to protect, and should never have been able to starve a real gate. |

Conflating them is how the bound gets quietly removed. AC2 above is written against the second
row only: no unit test should touch the host's real `rebar-gate-snapshots/locks`. Nothing in
this bug asks for the first row to change, and a patch that isolates real gate runs per session
should be rejected on sight.

**A sharper way to see it.** Today the failure is not merely noisy — a test suite can STARVE A
REAL GATE. While those 29 tests were failing they were also holding slots, so a genuine
`review-plan` on this box would have been refused by a test run. The production defect is the
starvation, not the red build; the red build is just how it announced itself.

## Method note that generalises beyond this bug

This was found because a `grep -cE "^(FAILED|ERROR)"` over colourised pytest output reported
"0 failures" for over an hour while 33 tests were failing: pytest emits ANSI escapes before
`FAILED`, so the pattern could never match. It is the same shape as the host-side defects this
session has been finding — a check whose passing condition is not the property it names.

**A monitor that has never produced a positive result is untested, not healthy.** Before
trusting a poller, feed it a known-bad line and confirm it fires.

compiled_state.description:
## Observed

`make verify` on 2026-09-06 failed with **33 failures, 29 of them identical**:

    rebar.llm.errors.GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent gate
    slot(s) on this host are in use

Affected files: `tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py` (17), `test_plan_review_reuse.py` (5),
`test_opcert_producer_seam_8d8e.py` (2), `workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py` (2),
`test_plan_review_cli_retry.py` (1, surfacing as `assert 11 == 2` — exit 11 is the transient
retry code), `test_plan_relation_snapshot.py` (1),
`test_completion_wrapper_duration_instrumentation.py` (1),
`interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_sign_transaction_lifecycle.py` (1).

## Root cause, established by measurement rather than inferred

It is NOT xdist contention. It reproduces **single-threaded, with `-p no:randomly -x`**.

The slot directory is host-wide:

    /var/folders/.../T/rebar-gate-snapshots/locks/gate-slot-{0,1,2,3}

`lsof` on those files during the failure named the holders, and none of them belonged to this
worktree:

    python3.1  7168  .../comment-gates-current/.venv/bin/rebar review-plan sphalerite-bereft-tortoise
    python3.1 14552  .../fix-caused-by-lagging-checkout/.venv/bin/pytest -n 4 ...
    (plus 48444, 85788, 90624)

So **another agent's `rebar review-plan`, and another agent's test run, in different
worktrees, were holding the slots this suite needs.** That is the admission bound working as
designed — it is a per-HOST bound (ADR 0112 decision 5), and `_slot_dir()` deliberately
follows `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` so the counter covers every process on the box.

The defect is that these TESTS opt into that shared bound. `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py`
does not have the problem: its `gate_host` fixture sets `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` to a `tmp_path`,
so it gets its own slot directory. The files above do not, so they inherit the real one.

## Why this matters beyond one red run

1. It makes `make verify` non-deterministic on any machine running more than one rebar
   process — which is this project's normal operating mode ("rebar is driven by MANY local
   agent processes at once"; bug `icicled-unstable-urial`).
2. It is indistinguishable, from the log alone, from a real regression. The failure is a
   `GateCongestedError` raised from production code, not a fixture error, so an author who
   has just touched anything gate-adjacent will reasonably suspect their own change. That
   cost was paid on story `cryptozoic-unlit-ladybug`.
3. `recheck`/re-run is the wrong response and AGENTS.md forbids it as a habit. The fix is
   isolation, not retry.

## Suggested fix

Give the affected modules the same `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` isolation `test_gate_admission_09da.py`
already uses. The narrow version is a fixture in each affected module; the better version is
one shared fixture, since the property wanted is "no unit test contends for the host's real
gate slots" rather than "these eight files do not".

Whether that fixture should be autouse across the unit suite needs care: `autouse_fixture` is
a censused kind under the shrink-only mechanism ratchet, so it needs a `mechanism-ok` marker
and a reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 The affected modules pass while another process on the same host holds all four
      real gate slots. Reproduce by taking the slots (e.g. a held `flock` on each
      `gate-slot-N`) and running the suite.
- [ ] AC2 No unit test acquires a slot in the host's real `rebar-gate-snapshots/locks`
      directory. A guard asserting this is preferable to fixing the eight files by hand.
- [ ] AC3 `tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py`'s own isolation is unchanged.

## NOT established

- Whether every one of the 29 failures has this single cause. They share the exception and
  the message, and the holders were foreign processes, but each was not individually traced.
- Whether the same contention affects the `integration`/`external` lanes.
compiled_state.title: Gate-exercising unit tests contend on the HOST-WIDE gate slot directory, so any concurrent rebar process on the same machine fails them
